draft.title: Economic activity and location
card: Industries choose sites that keep costs low and sales high. Four common pulls are resources, markets, transport and workers.
Resources
Industries that use heavy or bulky raw materials often locate near them. A mine, a quarry or a sawmill is usually close to its source, because moving the raw material is costly.
Markets and transport
Businesses that sell fresh or bulky goods often locate near their customers. Ports, railways and highways also attract industries, because they make moving goods cheaper and quicker.
Workers and technology

Industries that need skilled labour often locate where those workers live. New technology, such as refrigerated shipping or fast internet, can free a business from old limits, so patterns shift over time.
draft.remember: Industries locate where costs are low and sales are easy to reach, and new technology can change what that means.

a.q: Why is a sand and gravel quarry usually built close to the place where the sand and gravel are found?
opts: Moving heavy raw material over distance is costly
Quarry workers prefer to live in rural areas
Nearby customers want to buy directly from the pit
Ports cannot handle sand and gravel exports
a.why: Sand and gravel are heavy and cheap, so transporting them far would cost a lot compared with their value. Locating at the source keeps costs down. The customer option is tempting, but the card links raw material sites to the cost of moving the material, not to buyers visiting.
a.clue: Think about what it costs to move a heavy load.

b.q: A Sydney software firm hires skilled programmers who now work from home in towns across NSW over fast internet. Which idea does this best show?
opts: Technology can loosen the pull of a fixed location
Industries must always locate near their markets
Industries must always locate near raw materials
Transport costs matter more than ever for software
b.why: Fast internet lets the firm use workers far from its office, so the old need to be in one place weakens. The market option is wrong because the card says pulls are common, not fixed, and technology can change them.
b.clue: Ask what the internet has changed about where workers need to be.

a.best: Moving heavy raw material over distance is costly

b.best: Technology can loosen the pull of a fixed location

problems.detail: Two distractors say 'must always', which a student can rule out as absolute without knowing the idea. The right option is the only one with the hedge 'can', so it stands out.

check.summary: The card and question a are accurate and clear. In question b, the 'must always' distractors and the hedged right option make the answer easy to pick without understanding the idea.
